## Round 3 diff-only security review (HEAD d8d5eae0)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-a333eb5910a62a407.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-30T00:12:13.002Z

## Security Review Findings — round 3 (53703f8b..d8d5eae0, HEAD d8d5eae0)
All eight round-2 findings are fixed. I re-ran every round-2 payload list and about 200 new spellings through the hook at d8d5eae0, from the round-2 scratch repo. Every round-2 payload now asks. The named suite (`bash tests/run.sh e2e-tier-gate.test.sh`) exits 0 with 1816 passed and 0 failed.
### P1 — Critical Security Issues (Blocks Merge)
| **SEC-1 · security/bypass · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:886`**<br>This is a new regression: a GraphQL release mutation goes through without a prompt when an earlier string in the same query contains an odd number of escaped quotes. The stripper is written to handle `\"`, but a query typed on the command line reaches it only after `_bd_unescape_tok` (`lib/command-parse.sh:151`, called at `tier-gate.sh:1450`) has removed every backslash, quoted or not. So `body:"use a 6\" cable"` arrives as `body:"use a 6" cable"`, the string boundaries drift, and the next field name is read as string text. `gh api graphql -f query='mutation { updatePullRequest(input:{pullRequestId:"x", title:"Say \"hi"}) { clientMutationId } createRelease(input:{repositoryId:"x", tagName:"v9"}) { clientMutationId } }'` is allowed at d8d5eae0 and asked at 53703f8b. The `mergePullRequest` version is also allowed here, but block-unchecked-merge.sh still refuses it (tested); nothing else stops the release version. The same query in a file (`query=@q1.graphql`) asks. A double-quoted shell spelling (`\"...6\\\" cable\"`) was already allowed at 53703f8b. _(HIGH)_ | Give `_tg_gql_strip` the query text before backslashes are removed: take the `query=` value from the raw segment, or skip unescaping for that field. Alternatively, when a command-line query (`qs=0`) contains a `"` inside a string body, treat it as unreadable and let it ask. Add both payloads above to `e2e-tier-gate.test.sh`. |
### P2 — Security Concerns
| **SEC-2 · security/bypass · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1333`**<br>A redirection written with no space before it is never set aside. Bash splits on `>` and `<`, but the tokenizer does not, so the option and the redirection stay one word. `git push --tags>/dev/null`, `git push --follow-tags>/dev/null`, `git push --mirror>/dev/null`, `git push --tags</dev/null` and `git -c push.followTags=true push>/dev/null` are all allowed. A dry run in the scratch repo shows `git push -n --porcelain --tags>../o1.txt` sending both tags. `gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/1/merge>/dev/null` is allowed too (block-unchecked-merge is the backstop there). The header at line 209 says `>/dev/null` is set aside. This was already allowed at 53703f8b, but this round is the one that centralised redirection handling. _(HIGH)_ | In `_tg_drop_redirections`, split an unquoted word at its first unquoted `<` or `>` (with any fd digits or `&` in front), keep the part before as an argument, and drop the rest. Test with the payloads above. |
| **SEC-3 · security/bypass · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:640`**<br>A `git config` earlier in the same command is not read. The hook reads push.followTags, `remote.<n>.mirror`, `remote.<n>.push` and `remote.pushDefault` before the command runs, so `git config push.followTags true && git push`, `git config remote.origin.mirror true && git push`, `git config --add remote.origin.push 'refs/tags/*' && git push` and `git remote add m2 ../remote.git --mirror=push && git push m2` are all allowed. This is the same class as the env-var and `cd` cases this round fixed ("set or exported earlier in the same command"). The "Not covered" paragraph does not list it, so the header is inaccurate. Already allowed at 53703f8b. I did not run `git config` myself; that a stored config value applies to the next git process is standard git behaviour. _(HIGH)_ | Set the existing "configuration that may push tags" flag (`$4` of `_tg_git_push`), or the remote-choice flag, when an earlier simple command is `git config` / `git remote add\|set-url` naming push.*, remote.*, branch.*, include.* or includeIf.*. Otherwise list it under "Not covered". |
### P3 — Security Improvements
| **SEC-4 · security/bypass · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:446`**<br>`2>&1` in the middle of a command is split at its `&`, so the words after it become a separate command named `1`. `git push 2>&1 --tags`, `git push origin 2>&1 v1.0.0`, `gh release 2>&1 create v9` and `gh api 2>&1 -X POST repos/o/r/releases -f tag_name=v9` are all allowed. The dry run confirms `git push -n 2>&1 --tags` pushes tags. `2>&1` at the end of a command still works. The header (line 209) names `2>&1` as set aside. Placing it mid-command is unusual, hence P3. Already allowed at 53703f8b. _(HIGH)_ | Do not split segments at a `&` that directly follows `>` or `<` (`>&`, `<&`, `&>` are already handled as words). |
### Checked and not findings
### Summary
- `~/synapti-marketplace/plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh`
- `~/synapti-marketplace/plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh`

## Round 3 diff-only code review (HEAD d8d5eae0)

- Source: `<transcripts>/148019cc-de64-4bee-8c80-932a311792cc/subagents/agent-a0e5673bb3df6c2fe.jsonl` (final assistant message)
- Timestamp: 2026-10-30T00:13:08.155Z

## Code Review Findings: round 3, `53703f8b..d8d5eae0`, at HEAD d8d5eae0
### P1 — Critical (Blocks Merge)
| **F1 · security · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/lib/command-parse.sh:615`**<br>Pre-existing. When there is no space after `<<<`, the Tier 3 action is missed. `bash <<<'gh release create v9'`, `sh <<<"git push --tags"` and `bash 0<<<'gh pr merge 1'` all pass the tier gate without a prompt, at both 53703f8b and d8d5eae0. `block-unchecked-merge.sh` also lets `bash <<<'gh pr merge 1'` through (rc=0, while the spaced form gets rc=2). Cause: the tokenizer produces one word, `<<<gh release create v9`. `_bd_expand_interpreter_args` appends that word unchanged as a new command line. When that line is read again, `<<<gh` counts as a redirection (`_bd_is_redirection` `'<'*`, then `tier-gate.sh:1349` area), so the command word becomes `release`. The spaced form `bash <<< '...'` is caught. The header comment at `tier-gate.sh:209-211` says `<<<word` is set aside, and line 275 says "never a missed one". _(HIGH)_ | In `_bd_expand_interpreter_args`, strip a leading here-string operator (`<<<` or `[0-9]<<<`) from the word before appending it. Add e2e scenarios for the attached form, for both tier-gate and block-unchecked-merge. |
### P2 — Should Fix
| **F2 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1405`**<br>`cd ../wt && git push -u origin HEAD` asks, with a Tier 3 "may push or delete a tag" reason, when `../wt` is a worktree of the same repository. `git -C ../wt push -u origin HEAD` stays silent. `_tg_cd` compares `--show-toplevel`, and each worktree has its own. Tags and remote configuration are shared across worktrees, so the prompt adds no safety. Worktree lanes are how flow works in parallel. _(HIGH)_ | Compare `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` (resolved to an absolute path) instead of `--show-toplevel`. Another option: when the target can be read, judge the push in both repositories and keep the stricter result, which also covers another repository without a blanket prompt. |
### P3 — Consider
| **F4 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1386`**<br>Regression from base: `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git push` and `cd $REPO_ROOT && git push origin my-branch` now ask with a Tier 3 reason; base allowed both without a prompt. The header's list of variable targets covers this, but the paragraph on extra prompts (`:225-233`) does not, and this is a common way to start a command. None of flow's own command blocks do a `cd` before a push (grep of commands/skills/agents). _(HIGH)_ | Either treat a `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` target as the payload's top level, or list "a cd whose target is a variable or substitution" in the extra-prompt paragraph. |
| **F5 · performance · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1277`**<br>`_tg_scan` starts a separate `_tg_read_text` process for every quoted word that names gh or git after a program the hook does not know. With 200 quoted `'gh pr view N'` words the hook took 3.71s (base 0.09s); with 200 `'git log -n N'` words, 1.03s (base 0.27s). The command in `hooks.json` sets no timeout, so a much longer command could reach Claude Code's default limit. That limit's own behaviour was not checked here. Ordinary commands are unchanged: `git push` 0.215s vs base 0.224s, and `ls -la` 0.020s vs 0.021s. _(HIGH)_ | In `_tg_may_run`, also require gh, push, merge or release in the word before starting a process. Cap the number of quoted words read per simple command, the way `env -S` is capped at 8, and treat any overflow as `unknown`. |
| **F6 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1456`**<br>`_tg_git_env_name` is checked against every word, not only assignments. So `echo HOME && git push` and `unset GIT_DIR; git push` ask. _(HIGH)_ | Check only words that are assignments (`_tg_is_assignment`), whether written alone or after `export`, `declare` or `typeset`. |
| **F7 · correctness · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:1349`**<br>Round-2 finding not fully closed: `git push origin my-branch > "push log.txt"` and `2>"err log.txt"` still ask, because a redirection target that contains a space is kept as a refspec. After a standalone operator, the next word is the target whether or not it is quoted. _(HIGH)_ | After a standalone operator, always consume the next word. If the here-string text needs reading, handle that in the `<<<` arm (see F1). |
| **F9 · duplication · `plugins/flow/hooks/scripts/tier-gate.sh:927`**<br>`_tg_pflag_short` and the short-option branch of `_tg_wrapper_opt` (`:410`) are the same letter-by-letter bundle parser, apart from `=value`. Both are new in this range. _(MEDIUM)_ | Use one helper with a flag for whether `=value` is accepted. |
### What I checked and what held
- **Test suites** (exit status read before any filtering): `bash tests/run.sh e2e-tier-gate.test.sh` gave rc=0, pass=1816, fail=0. `e2e-release-versions.test.sh` gave rc=0, pass=533, fail=0.
- **Not run:** a differential run of the new tier-gate scenarios against the 53703f8b hook, so I have not shown that each new scenario fails on base.
### Summary
- Files reviewed: 13 (the full diff, focusing on `tier-gate.sh`, `command-parse.sh`, `release.md` and the two test files).
  - `_bd_unescape_tok`: 3 (git grep; tier-gate.sh ×2, block-unchecked-merge.sh ×1).
  - `_bd_expand_interpreter_args`: 3 hooks (git grep). F1 affects block-unchecked-merge too; block-destructive was not probed.
